details: Outpost Zero – Design. Deploy. Survive. Outpost Zero is an interactive space-survival simulation that allows users to establish and manage a human outpost on the Moon or Mars. The objective is to keep a crew of four members alive for 30 mission days while managing limited resources and handling challenging environmental conditions. How It Works Users select a Moon or Mars mission, choose their difficulty level, and deploy modules to build their outpost. They must manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, electricity, credits, and mass. The simulation engine calculates daily resource consumption, power generation, environmental hazards, equipment failures, and crew survival conditions. Users can monitor mission progress, respond to warnings, adjust resource priorities, and make strategic decisions. Technology Used The project is developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Zustand. We use a deterministic simulation engine with a seeded pseudo-random number generator (Mulberry32) to produce reproducible mission outcomes. NASA's DONKI API is integrated to incorporate Solar Energetic Particle event data into radiation-related mission scenarios. A bundled historical dataset provides fallback data when the API is unavailable. We also developed Lunar Escape, a standalone 2D mini-game using the HTML Canvas API. Players collect six oxygen crystals, avoid meteors, and reach a safe habitat. For quality assurance, we use Vitest for unit testing, Playwright for end-to-end testing, and ESLint for code quality. Benefits and Intended Impact Outpost Zero provides an engaging way to understand the challenges of space exploration, resource allocation, environmental risks, and decision-making under limited resources. It encourages strategic thinking, problem-solving, and awareness of the systems required to sustain human life beyond Earth. It is designed as an educational simulation, not a real-world spacecraft survival prediction system. Creativity and Innovation The project combines resource-management simulation, deterministic mission generation, space-weather information, and an interactive mini-game in one experience. Its reproducible scenarios allow users to experiment with different strategies and compare mission outcomes. Factors Considered Our team considered resource limitations, crew survival, environmental hazards, mission duration, simulation consistency, user experience, API reliability, and software testing. We also focused on keeping the interface interactive and easy to understand. Our vision is to make the challenges of establishing a human settlement beyond Earth more accessible through technology, simulation, and interactive learning.
